statement: Worst-case reading of the record: taking, for every one of the 11 experiments, the lower of (survival table, weight-implied survivors) for PSLN-344 and the higher of the two for PSLN-212 gives 66 of 80 (82%; 95% CI 72–90%) vs 15 of 80 (19%; 95% CI 11–29%); Fisher p = 2×10⁻¹⁶.
Aged PSLN-344 vs the young PSLN-212 benchmark in the 10 experiments that had both arms: 58/70 (83%) vs 69/70 (99%); risk difference -16 points (95% CI -24 to -7); stratified log-rank p = 0.001.

Restoration index (RI) of PSLN-344 in aged animals = (PSLN-344 aged - PSLN-212 aged) / (PSLN-212 young - PSLN-212 aged), computed for the 40 read-outs that have all three groups: median 0.71 (range 0.17–0.98); by domain: interferon 0.98, monocyte/DC 0.71, germinal centre/Tfh 0.67, antibody 0.74, CD8 T cell 0.62. 17 of 40 read-outs remain significantly different from young (Welch p < 0.05, unadjusted).

statement: Dendritic-cell co-stimulation, lymph node day 3 (% positive, mean of 5): CD40 aged PSLN-212 5.6, aged PSLN-344 11.2, young PSLN-212 38.7 (RI 0.17, 95% CI 0.09–0.26); CD86 8.1, 14.5, 37.9 (RI 0.22, 0.13–0.30). The lowest restoration of any read-out.

Durability in aged animals: PSLN-344 survival 20 of 21 (95%; 95% CI 76–100%) when challenged on day 14 (S03-I, S06-A, S06-C) vs 14 of 21 (67%; 95% CI 43–85%) when challenged on day 60 (S06-E, S06-F, S06-G); Fisher exact p = 0.045. CDN-1807 vs cGAMP in the same liposome without Mn²⁺ (aged animals): lung Ifnb1 at 16 h geometric mean 16.5 (PSLN-212) vs 7.7 (CMP-204), ratio 2.2 (95% CI 1.6–2.8; Tukey p = 0.001). HAI GMT against CA09 46 vs 23 (Tukey p = 0.16, not significant). Survival after CA09 challenge (S03-I, as printed): CMP-204 3 of 7, PSLN-212 0 of 7 - but the control-arm labels of S03-I are in doubt.

Design facts taken from the annotation file (page 1 and block entries): BALB/c animals were female and the sex of the C57BL/6 and Swiss Webster animals is not stated; aged = 20 months or older (BALB/c), 20 months (C57BL/6, Swiss Webster); young = 7–8 weeks; vaccines were whole virus inactivated with 0.02% formalin; every challenge study used a single intranasal dose of 20 µg adjuvant; groups were 5 animals (most immune read-outs), 3 (some) or 7–10 (challenge studies). The file contains no statement of randomisation or blinding, no virus-titre data, no histopathology, no pharmacokinetics, no manganese measurement and no species other than mouse.

statement: Lung inflammatory transcripts (S09-A; geometric-mean fold vs untreated, n = 3). 16 h: PSLN-344 aged Il6 36, Tnf 40, Ccl2 590; young PSLN-212 60, 14, 1391. Second panel (printed '16h'; its Ifnb1 row reproduces the 72 h values of S01-A, so I treat it as 72 h): PSLN-344 aged Il6 7.2, Tnf 8.4, Ccl2 27, Il10 4.2; aged PSLN-212 1.9, 5.2, 5.2, 4.2; young PSLN-212 3.1, 0.5, 102, 0.1; PSLN-212/R848 34, 50, 58, 45.

Resolution of the lung response in aged PSLN-344 animals is incomplete at the last time points sampled: lung monocytes on day 8 18.4% (vehicle 9.5%, young PSLN-212 14.1%; Tukey p vs young = 0.0003); CD11b+ dendritic cells on day 8 13.7% (vehicle 2.4%, young 9.5%); Ifnb1 at 72 h 4.4-fold (young PSLN-212 1.6-fold). No sample later than day 8 for these read-outs.

Antigen requirement (S15-H, aged, rgH5N1 challenge 3 days after dosing): vaccine alone 0 of 7 survived, PSLN-344 alone 0 of 7, vaccine + PSLN-344 6 of 7 (Fisher p = 0.005 vs either single component). Adjuvant alone did not shorten survival relative to vaccine alone (median day of death 6 vs 5; log-rank exact p = 0.31).

Morbidity after challenge (lowest body weight per animal, % of day 0, averaged over the 10 aged-animal challenge blocks with weight records): PSLN-344 aged 87.1%, young PSLN-212 90.3%, aged PSLN-212 82.2%. PSLN-344 animals lost more weight than the young benchmark in 10 of 10 blocks (paired t across blocks p = 2×10⁻⁶). Weight blocks contain re-used traces (record defect D7) and are supporting evidence only.

Dose-response of lung Ifnb1 at 16 h (S08-A; 1, 5, 10, 20, 40 µg; n = 3 per dose; age of animals not stated): PSLN-344 means 1.4, 8.3, 21.1, 45.8, 50.2; PSLN-212 1.4, 4.1, 8.9, 12.6, 14.9; CMP-204 1.0, 3.8, 6.3, 7.3, 8.0. Hill fit: maximum effect 59-fold (95% CI 49–70) for PSLN-344 vs 17 (14–20) for PSLN-212; half-maximal dose 13 µg (11–17) vs 11 µg. Doubling the dose from 20 to 40 µg adds 10%. No survival, antibody or tolerability data at any dose other than 20 µg.
analysis: a10_dose_response.py -> T14 (least squares on log scale; bootstrap CI)

statement: Young animals (three challenge studies, S09-B, S09-D, S09-F; challenge 21–180 days after one dose): PSLN-344 24 of 24 survived, PSLN-212 24 of 24, vehicle 0 of 23. No survival difference between the two formulations in young animals.

Sample size (two-sided Fisher exact test, alpha 0.05): to detect 75% vs 25% survival needs 18 per group for 80% power and 23 for 90%; the observed 84% vs 12% needs 11 for 90%; 80% vs 40% (an attribution arm) needs 27; a day-14 vs day-60 difference of 93% vs 67% needs 40. With 24 per group the power for 75% vs 25% is 93% and for 80% vs 40% is 76%. The historical design (7 per group) had 69% power for the observed effect and 3% for the durability difference.

statement: Precision of a background-mortality estimate: if 19% of unchallenged aged controls die, a group of 7 gives a 95% CI of 0–58% (1/7) and a group of 20 gives 6–44% (4/20).

Antibody on day 14 after one dose, geometric mean titre (n = 5), vehicle / aged PSLN-212 / aged PSLN-344 / young PSLN-212: IgG anti-CA09 56 / 393 / 7305 / 11959; neutralising anti-CA09 52 / 418 / 3840 / 6686; IgG anti-Aichi 52 / 426 / 5701 / 13855. After a booster (day 28): IgG anti-CA09 4411 / 15651 / 40739; anti-Aichi 1086 / 12435 / 43472 (aged PSLN-344 = 38% and 29% of young).

Encapsulation efficiency (S08-B, n = 3 preparations, mean ± SD): CMP-204 65.2 ± 6.0%, PSLN-212 59.6 ± 4.6%, PSLN-R848 61.3 ± 6.8%, PSLN-212/R848 52.4 ± 7.3%, PSLN-344 54.8 ± 5.1%. The only formulation-quality data in the package: particle size, charge, manganese content, stability and endotoxin are described as measured but are not in the workbook.

In young animals Mn²⁺ adds little: Ifnb1 at 16 h 50.7- vs 37.6-fold (ratio 1.34; Tukey p = 0.63); antigen-carrying DC 11.1% vs 9.4%; cross-priming 31.4% vs 26.2% (both not significant); survival 24 of 24 vs 24 of 24; lowest body weight after challenge 89.7% vs 88.9%, 90.7% vs 89.5%, 87.3% vs 89.3% (S09-C, E, G).

Middle-aged animals (14 months at vaccination: infected or mock-infected at 10 months, vaccinated 4 months later; two challenge studies): previously uninfected animals survived 0 of 14 with PSLN-212 and 12 of 14 with PSLN-344 (Fisher p = 6×10⁻⁶).

Wild-type H5N1 challenge 2 days after one dose (S03-J): PSLN-344 10 of 10 survived (9 records carry a day value, 1 has the survival flag but an empty day cell); the two control arms survived 1 of 10 and 3 of 10 (printed 'Sham' and 'PSLN-212'; the paired weight block S13-G labels its arms 'Naive' and 'Sham').

Prior influenza exposure ('imprinting' with PR8 H1N1 four months before vaccination): PSLN-344 protected 12 of 14 previously infected and 12 of 14 previously uninfected animals; PSLN-212 protected 4 of 14 previously infected animals (all 4 survivors in the PR8 re-challenge, 0 of 7 against Perth H3N2).

Vehicle function. Alveolar macrophages taking up dye-labelled liposome at 16 h: wild-type 43.1% vs surfactant-protein A/D knock-out 12.7% (n = 4; Welch p = 4×10⁻⁵). Dye-positive alveolar epithelial cells after liposomal vs free dye: type II 15.8% vs 0.38%; type I 3.8% vs 0.33% (n = 5; Tukey p < 0.01 for both).
Gap-junction blocker carbenoxolone before vaccine + PSLN-344: recruited lung monocytes on day 3 3.1% vs 7.3% without blocker (-58%; n = 5; Welch p = 0.004).
Lung Gm-csf transcript (fold vs untreated, mean of 5) at 16 / 36 / 72 h: PSLN-344 6.0 / 8.7 / 3.9; PSLN-212 1.5 / 1.6 / 1.4; vehicle 1.0 / 1.2 / 1.2 (aged animals; Tukey p < 0.001 at each time).

Lung monocytes (% of lung cells, mean of 5) on day 4: vehicle 10.4, aged PSLN-212 16.7, aged PSLN-344 30.6, young PSLN-212 32.2 (Tukey p, PSLN-344 vs PSLN-212 = 2×10⁻⁵). CCR2 antagonist INCB3344 before vaccine + PSLN-344: monocytes 9.9% -> 3.3%, Ly6C+ macrophages 15.4% -> 2.5% (n = 5; Welch p <= 0.003; time point not stated).

Monocyte-to-dendritic-cell conversion after vaccine + PSLN-344 (donor-derived monocyte-derived DC, %, mean of 5): wild-type marrow 19.7, interferon-receptor-deficient marrow 2.1 (-89%; Tukey p < 0.0001), receptor-deficient marrow + GM-CSF 12.4 (S02-H). In aged PSLN-212 animals GM-CSF raised monocyte-derived DC-like cells from 5.9% to 13.8% (Tukey p = 0.0001; S02-G). Monocyte entry itself was not clearly interferon-receptor dependent: 21.3% vs 15.4% (n = 3; Welch p = 0.12; S12-A).

Dendritic cells, aged PSLN-344 vs aged PSLN-212 (young PSLN-212 in brackets), mean of 5: lung CD11b+ DC day 4 18.9% vs 8.3% (21.4%); lung cDC1 at 72 h 37.5% vs 22.8% (43.4%); CCR7+ migratory DC 30.7% vs 7.3% (35.0%); lymph-node CD11b+ DC 36.8% vs 18.2% (44.7%); antigen-carrying DC in lymph node at 36 h 7.1% vs 1.8% (9.4%), 2.4% with pertussis toxin (the adjuvant given to the PTX group is not stated). All PSLN-344 vs PSLN-212 Tukey p < 0.01.

Cross-priming capacity of lymph-node DC (proliferation of naive OT-I CD8 T cells in co-culture, %, mean of 5): aged PSLN-212 0.8, aged PSLN-344 18.7, young PSLN-212 26.2, young PSLN-344 31.4; pertussis-toxin group 2.5.

Germinal-centre response in the draining lymph node, aged PSLN-344 vs aged PSLN-212 (young PSLN-212): GC B cells day 7 6.5% vs 2.3% (9.8%); ICOS-high follicular helper T cells 10.3% vs 3.8% (13.6%); follicular regulatory T cells 10.8% vs 26.7% (7.1%); helper:regulatory ratio 8.5 vs 2.9 (16.0); Aicda transcript 12.0- vs 3.4-fold (n = 3); IgG+ B cells 25.9% vs 11.2% (27.1%). By day 30 follicular regulatory cells no longer differ: 14.0% vs 18.0% (vehicle 13.9%; young 7.4%; Tukey p = 0.14 vs PSLN-212).

IgG2a/IgG1 ratio (a marker of a type-1-skewed antibody response) recomputed from the subclass titres in S13-A..D (mean of 5): anti-CA09 aged PSLN-212 0.58, aged PSLN-344 2.14, young PSLN-212 2.97; anti-Aichi 0.51, 2.73, 2.89. The ratio blocks S03-B and S03-F contain exactly these 15 + 15 values but under headers rotated by one position (as printed they would read PSLN-212 2.97, PSLN-344 0.58, young 2.14).

statement: Lung CD8 T cells. Transferred OT-I cells proliferated in the lung whether or not lymph-node trafficking was blocked with pertussis toxin (59% vs 55%), while proliferation in the lymph node fell from 31% to 7% (n = 3; S05-C). Day 3 after vaccination, aged PSLN-344 vs aged PSLN-212 (young): Ki-67+ CD8 9.4% vs 3.5% (9.9%); granzyme-B+ CD8 5.7% vs 3.0% (9.6%). Blocking CCR2 in young PSLN-344 animals cut granzyme-B+ CD8 from 6.8% to 1.4% (n = 5; Welch p = 0.0001; S02-I).
Lung-resident memory CD8 T cells on day 25 (%, mean of 5): vehicle 0.6, aged PSLN-212 1.0, aged PSLN-344 4.0, young PSLN-212 6.0 (Tukey p, PSLN-344 vs PSLN-212 < 0.0001; vs young = 3×10⁻⁵).

Suppressive lung environment of aged animals: CD206+ macrophages vehicle 85%, aged PSLN-212 71%, aged PSLN-344 49%, young PSLN-212 36% (n = 5; time point not stated; S11-E); lung regulatory T cells day 7 5.9%, 6.7%, 3.0%, 1.8% (n = 3; S04-D). Ly6C+CCR2+ macrophages accumulated after PSLN-212 but not PSLN-344 (19.0 vs 3.4 ×10⁵ cells on day 5; n = 3; S07-A). A macrophage-transfer experiment changed lung regulatory T cells (10.4% vs 5.1%) but both columns carry the same label, so the direction cannot be assigned (S07-C).

Does adding Mn²⁺ change delivery to the epithelium? S08-C as printed: type II cells 15.8% (liposome) vs 3.8% (Mn liposome); type I 13.8% vs 3.0% - a four- to five-fold loss. But S01-B gives 3.8% for type I cells with the same liposome, which equals S08-C column B (3.8%), not column C (13.8%). If columns B and C are transposed, the Mn liposome delivers 13.8% (type II) and 3.0% (type I), i.e. no material loss. Unresolved.
Gm-csf at 16 h separates aged PSLN-344 (lowest animal 5.4-fold) from aged PSLN-212 (highest animal 2.0-fold); no young group in this block.

An HAI titre of 40 did not mark protection in aged animals: all 5 aged PSLN-212 animals reached 40 or more against CA09 (values 40, 80, 40, 40, 40), yet the PSLN-212 group was not protected against CA09 challenge (0 of 7 in S03-I as printed; 3 of 7 if the paired weight block is right). Every animal in the two protective regimens had HAI of 160 or more.

Challenge studies in the file: 12 in aged animals (S03-I, S03-J, S06-A, -B, -C, -D, -E, -F, -G, S15-H, S15-L, S15-N), 2 in 14-month-old animals (S06-E and S06-F, rows 71-105), 4 in young animals (S09-B, S09-D, S09-F, S13-E).

Outbred Swiss Webster (S15-N): PSLN-344 6 of 7 vs PSLN-212 2 of 7 - not significant on its own (log-rank exact p = 0.09; Fisher p = 0.10); vs vehicle 0 of 7, p = 0.003. Individual experiments have 7 animals per group; several PSLN-344 vs PSLN-212 contrasts are individually borderline, and the conclusion rests on the pooled analysis.
